questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to choose a destination that really interested me. I chose Milan in Italy for my love for Italian culture, food, history and language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All study related information, and information about the socializing Erasmus Student Network, was all sent directly to me before my stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned a Buddy through the Erasmus Student Network that could help me answer questions about university and general questions about the city/country.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through AirBnB. Although quite expensive, having an apartment closer to the city center and university gave a lot of freedom; both in relation to placement and movement, but also in relation to the rules that might be on On-Campus housing / dormitories.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is typically more expensive than on-campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
After having been granted, and accepted, the spot, I received an Email from the university with an online application formula, easy to fill out. 
This formula includes filling out the courses the student wishes to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the technical details, about semester start dates, deadlines, academic coordinators and department, was all given in this Email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I found out relatively late that my preferred courses were overlapping a bit. So I continued my search for courses after lectures began, and could easily change a course. It would seem that very few courses had a limited number of spots.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have multiple courses in mind when you search, in the case that you cannot / will not attend one of the courses in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I was a Bachelor student when going to Milan. In Milan, Bachelor courses are taught Italian and Masters courses taught in English. 
Therefore I chose 3 Masters courses and 1 bachelor course (given that I knew some Italian and was able to follow the classes). This meant that the academic level was a bit higher that what I was used to, but in the end, the difference was not big.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Attending university in Milan, in my experience, was solely attending lectures. 
There was no books to read before lectures and no assignments to do before or after lectures. 
This of course meant a lot free time, but the end, I found exam studying quite difficult, given the limited number of resources (only lecture slides). 
Compared to in Copenhagen, where we have lectures, seminars (with assignments), and previous exams to use as exam training, the University in Milan lacks a lot of learning methods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Molecular Analysis and Traceability of Biotechnological Products
Biologia Molecolare (Molecular Biology)
Molecular and Cellular Microbiology
Molecular Pharmacology and Immunology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Molecular Pharmacology and Immunology was a very interesting two-part course, having one exam in Pharmacology and one exam in Immunology, Lectures were very interesting, and was the course I had the most fun with.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport in the city was much less expensive than expected (22 euro pr. month + 10 euro for a travel card (one time purchase)). 
Additionally, food in supermarkets were quite cheap as well. 
Housing was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The university itself provides some sports clubs, that I did not attend, but looked quite interesting (volley + football championships for example). 
The Erasmus Student Network provided endless opportunities to socialize - dinners, sports events, spontaneous meetings and what not. Definitely the best way to meet both locals and other exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many announcements on campus for sports clubs, theater clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Organize trips to other cities in Italy as well. The train networks are really good, and it is so easy to arrange one-day trips to other cities. 
Milan has a lot to offer as well, so be a tourist in your own city as often as you can.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mostly easy. The toughest part was adjusting to their not-so-strict relationship with time, with most Italians being late for appointments.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to a lot of events in the beginning - you are sure to find someone you click with, and the locals really want to help you on your way as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The student-teacher relationship. The professors are addressed as Professor followed by last name, and if you speak in Italian to a Professor, they are addressed in the formal way of speaking. This was not challenging, but definitely a significant cultural difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The spontaneous meetings hosted so often, such as meeting for a coffee or a drink, or watching sport on the local bar in the evening.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do it, even if you're scared. I was. 
Attend the social activities early on.
Even though the study is important, and much time should be used on that, get to explore the country and culture as much as possible - it is an experience you'll never forget.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend lessons and start to study early on as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my Italian language level as time went, understanding new words used often in the daily use.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The self discipline needed to study on your own - the habits you have for studying at home (such as your good study partners) are not all applicable in the way the study is taught on the host university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Buon viaggio :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
